message.content:
This is a clad disc of stainless steel (55% by weight) and aluminum (45%), used as a cookware blank. The relevant heading is 7410 or 7606 for aluminum, or 7219/7220 for stainless flat-rolled products. Under Section XV Note 7 and the Chapter 72/76 rules, composite goods are classified by the metal that predominates by weight, which here is stainless steel at 55%.

Stainless steel discs: Chapter 72 covers flat-rolled products, and heading 7220 covers flat-rolled stainless products less than 600 mm wide. A circle is a flat-rolled product cut to shape, and CBP has ruled that clad discs fall in 7220. For example, NY rulings on 3-ply and 5-ply discs for cookware classify them in 7220.20 or 7220.90. Clad products fall under Note 1(k) of Chapter 72, where the classification is by the predominant metal. Since the diameter is 300 mm (under 600 mm) and the thickness is 3 mm (over 3 mm is not met, as it is exactly 3), the subheading is 7220.20 (cold-rolled) or 7220.90 (other). The clad disc is cold-rolled or cold-finished, so 7220.20. Within 7220.20, thickness under 4.75 mm falls under 7220.20.10 (not further worked than cold-rolled), and the statistical suffix for 7220.20.1000 or 7220.20.7005 etc. is uncertain.

The 7220.20 subheadings are:
- 7220.20.10: not further worked than cold-rolled (cold-reduced)
- 7220.20.60: not cut, not in coils, 4.75 mm or more... (I'm not sure of these)
- 7220.20.70: other, thickness 4.75 mm or more
- 7220.20.80: other, thickness under 4.75 mm
- 7220.20.8000 and further 7220.20.8060 for other items.

The best choice is 7220.20.8000, though 7220.20.1000 is also possible. Since the disc is clad and further worked, I choose 7220.20.8000.
